items.title: 2.3.2 Derivative of a Function Given in the Form of Parametric Equations (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 37-38: derivative of a function given by parametric equations x = f(t), y = g(t) via the chain rule; Example 4

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Kabhi kabhi curve ko seedha y = (x ka formula) ki shakal mein dena mushkil hota hai. Socho ek cricket ball hawa mein ja rahi hai: us ki ufqi (horizontal) doori x bhi waqt ke saath badalti hai aur oonchai y bhi. Dono ko waqt t mein likhna aasan hai. Aisi equations ko parametric equations kehte hain. Aaj hum seekhenge ke in se dy/dx kaise nikalte hain, aur woh bhi t ko khatam kiye baghair.

Kitab ke mutabiq: maan lijiye function parametric equations se diya gaya hai
\[x = f(t) \quad \text{aur} \quad y = g(t)\]
\(x = f(t)\) se humein milta hai
\[t = f^{-1}(x)\]
(basharte \(f\) bijective ho, yani one-one aur onto)
Ab \(y = g(t)\) aur \(t = f^{-1}(x)\) par Chain Rule lagane se:
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy}{dt} \cdot \dfrac{dt}{dx}\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\;\frac{dy}{dt}\;}{\frac{dx}{dt}}\]
\(\left(\because \frac{dt}{dx} = \frac{1}{dx/dt}\right)\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
'Parametric' ka matlab: \(x\) aur \(y\) ke darmiyan ek equation dene ke bajaye dono ko ek teesre variable \(t\) mein diya jata hai. Is \(t\) ko parameter kehte hain. \(t\) ko waqt samjho aur \((x, y)\) ko chalte hue point ki position: \(t\) ki har value curve ka ek point deti hai.
\(f\) bijective kyun ho? Taa ke har \(x\) sirf ek hi \(t\) se aaye. Tab \(t = f^{-1}(x)\) mojood hota hai aur \(y\) sach mein \(x\) ka function banta hai.
\(\frac{dt}{dx} = \frac{1}{dx/dt}\) kyun? Agar \(x\), \(t\) ke muqable mein 3 guna tez badalta hai, to \(t\), \(x\) ke muqable mein 3 ka ulta, yani \(\frac{1}{3}\) guna badlega. Shart: \(\frac{dx}{dt} \ne 0\).
Faida kya hai? Humein \(f^{-1}\) kabhi nikalna hi nahin parta. Bas \(x\) aur \(y\) ko \(t\) ke lihaaz se differentiate karo aur taqseem kar do.

blocks.text_alt: dy by dx barabar hai dy by dt taqseem dx by dt, basharte dx by dt zero na ho

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Find \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) if \(y = a\cos t\) and \(x = a\sin t\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = a\cos t\), \(x = a\sin t\). Yeh parametric equations hain jin ka parameter \(t\) hai.
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: \(x\) aur \(y\) dono \(t\) mein diye hain, aur \(y\) seedha \(x\) mein nahin. Is liye dono ko \(t\) ke lihaaz se differentiate karenge aur phir taqseem: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}\).

Step 1: Dono equations ko t ke lihaaz se differentiate karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -a\sin t\]
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = a\cos t\]
Kyun: \(a\) constant hai, woh apni jagah rehta hai; \((\cos t)' = -\sin t\) aur \((\sin t)' = \cos t\).
Dhyan dein: \(\cos\) ke derivative ka minus yahan sab se zyada bhoola jata hai.

Step 2: Chain Rule lagayein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}\]
\[= -\dfrac{a\sin t}{a\cos t}\]
\[= -\tan t\]
Kyun: \(a\) upar neeche se cancel hua (\(a \ne 0\)), aur \(\frac{\sin t}{\cos t} = \tan t\). Shart: \(\cos t \ne 0\), warna neeche zero aa jata.

Tasdeeq: \(t\) ko khatam kar ke dekhein: \(x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}\sin^{2} t + a^{2}\cos^{2} t = a^{2}\). Yeh circle hai! Is ko implicitly (2.3.3 wala tareeqa) differentiate karein: \(2x + 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\), is liye
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y} = -\dfrac{a\sin t}{a\cos t}\]
\[= -\tan t\]
Do alag raaston se ek hi jawab: yaqeen pakka.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(a) \(x = t^{2}\), \(y = t^{3}\): \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 3t^{2}\), \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 2t\), is liye \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3t^{2}}{2t} = \frac{3t}{2}\) (\(t \ne 0\)). Ek \(t\) cancel ho gaya.
(b) \(x = a\cos t\), \(y = b\sin t\) (yeh ellipse hai): \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{b\cos t}{-a\sin t} = -\frac{b}{a}\cot t\) (\(\sin t \ne 0\)). Agar \(a = b\) ho to yeh circle ban jata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 4 mein \(t = 0\) par slope kya hai? \(-\tan 0 = 0\). Us waqt point \((0, a)\) hai, yani circle ki sab se oonchi jagah. Kya wahan tangent ufqi (seedha leta hua) nahin hona chahiye? Bilkul, aur slope 0 yahi batata hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Parametric form: \(x = f(t)\), \(y = g(t)\); \(t\) parameter hai.
2. \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}\), basharte \(\frac{dx}{dt} \ne 0\); yeh chain rule se nikalta hai.
3. Jawab aam taur par \(t\) mein hi chhor dete hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Ulta divide kar dena: \(\frac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}\) to \(\frac{dx}{dy}\) hai, \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nahin. Yaad rakhein: jo upar chahiye (\(y\)) woh upar.
2. \((\cos t)' = -\sin t\) ka minus bhool jana.
3. Woh points nazar andaaz karna jahan \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 0\) ho (Example 4 mein jahan \(\cos t = 0\)).
